- Diagnostic yield **82–99%** (immunocompetent), lower in AIDS (56–96%)
- **Enhancing lesions ≈ 99%** vs. non-enhancing ≈ 74%

cards.vorderseite: DBS beyond Parkinson's, tremor and dystonia
cards.rueckseite:
- **Epilepsy:** bilateral **anterior nucleus of the thalamus** (SANTE: 68% had ≥ 50% fewer seizures at 5 y)
- **OCD:** anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC)/STN
- **Tourette syndrome:** GPi, STN, ALIC
- **Depression:** subgenual cingulate, anterior capsule
- **Pain:** sensory thalamus, periaqueductal/periventricular gray (25–60% respond)
Contraindications: significant **dementia**, bleeding risk (coagulopathy, uncontrolled hypertension).

cards.vorderseite: Intrathecal baclofen: test dose and pump selection
cards.rueckseite:
- Indication: severe spasticity **refractory to oral drugs** or intolerable side effects
- **Test bolus** via LP: 50 → 75 → 100 mcg (vs. placebo); positive = **≥ 2-point Ashworth reduction for ≥ 4 h**
- Pump only if response at **≤ 100 mcg**, no allergy
- Catheter usually in at L2–3, tip advanced ≈ 3 levels
- Danger: **abrupt withdrawal** (high fever, rebound spasticity, seizures, rhabdomyolysis, death) and overdose (respiratory depression, coma)

- First line: **botulinum toxin** (good for retrocollis, poorer for lateral torticollis)
- **Selective peripheral denervation:** section of the spinal accessory nerve branch to SCM + posterior rami C1–C6 (Bertrand), including the anastomoses between XI and upper cervical roots
- **GPi DBS** for refractory cervical dystonia
Exclude secondary causes (e.g., atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation, posterior fossa tumor).

cards.titel: Choosing a pain procedure for refractory cancer pain
cards.notiz: Greenberg p. 1877–1878. Prerequisite: maximized systemic opioids. Nonablative before ablative procedures. Mesencephalotomy: lesion 5 mm lateral to the aqueduct at inferior colliculus level; complication = vertical gaze/diplopia.

cards.rueckseite:
Interrupts crossing pain fibers in the anterior commissure over the segments involved → for **bilateral or midline (pelvic, perineal, visceral) pain**.
Results: complete relief 60%, partial 28%.
Complications: dysesthesias and impaired joint position sense (dorsal column injury, ≈ 16%), leg weakness ≈ 8%, **bladder dysfunction ≈ 12%**, sexual dysfunction.

- **Trial first:** epidural 5–10 mg or intrathecal **0.5–2 mg morphine** (preservative-free)
- Intrathecal doses ≈ **5–10× lower** than epidural; epidural catheters scar and fail sooner
- Implantable pump if **life expectancy > 3 months**
- Cancer pain improves in **up to 90%**, neuropathic pain only 25–50%
- Risks: delayed **respiratory depression** (monitor rate hourly × 24 h), tolerance, catheter problems, granuloma
Intraventricular morphine (0.5–1 mg via reservoir) for head/neck cancer pain.

cards.vorderseite: Spinal cord stimulation: indications, trial and complications
cards.rueckseite:
- **FDA indications:** **failed back surgery syndrome** (esp. leg > back pain), **CRPS**
- Other: refractory angina, painful limb ischemia, neuropathic pain
- Relative contraindication: psychosis, untreated psychiatric illness, drug-seeking
- **Trial** with external generator; success = **> 50% pain reduction**
- Device complications ≈ **32%**: **lead migration 13%**, breakage 9%, infection 3.5%
- Long-term success ≈ 74%

**Purpose:** lateralize **language** and test whether the hemisphere opposite the planned resection can sustain **memory** on its own.
Technique: 100–125 mg sodium amobarbital into one ICA → contralateral hemiplegia; test speech and memory (pictures/objects), then the other side.
Recommended in **left-handed** patients; may be inaccurate with high-flow AVMs or cross-filling. Increasingly replaced by fMRI.

cards.titel: Engel classification of epilepsy surgery outcome
zeilen: Free of disabling seizures (I-A completely seizure-free; auras/simple partial allowed in I-B)
cards.notiz: Greenberg p. 1895. ILAE outcome classes 1–6 are an alternative (class 1 = completely seizure-free, no auras).

cards.vorderseite: Risks of temporal lobe epilepsy surgery
cards.rueckseite:
- **Contralateral superior quadrantanopia** ("pie in the sky", Meyer's loop): the most common deficit
- **Hemiparesis** from **anterior choroidal artery** injury (mesial resection) or Sylvian branches
- **CN III** injury (medial to the tentorial edge during hippocampectomy)
- Language/memory deficits (dominant side)
**LITT** (MRI-guided laser ablation) of mesial structures: less invasive alternative, seizure freedom ≈ 50–80% in small series.

cards.vorderseite: Radiation injury of the brain: time course and late effects
cards.rueckseite:
- **Acute** (during treatment): edema, worsening of existing symptoms → steroids
- **Early delayed** (weeks to 3 months): somnolence/lethargy, memory problems; in the cord **Lhermitte sign**; reversible
- **Late delayed** (3 months–12 years, mostly < 3 y): **radiation necrosis** (small-vessel injury), white matter atrophy
Other late effects: cognitive decline (children lose up to 25 IQ points), hypopituitarism, hypothyroidism, **radiation-induced tumors** (meningioma, glioma, nerve sheath tumors), vasculopathy, leukoencephalopathy with methotrexate.
Treatment of necrosis: steroids, **bevacizumab**, resection if mass effect.

Follows radiation of nearby cancers (lung, breast, thyroid, head and neck).
- **Type 1:** transient, benign, months after RT: Lhermitte sign only, resolves
- **Type 2:** anterior horn cell injury → lower motor neuron signs
- **Type 3:** acute complete lesion (experimental only)
- **Type 4:** chronic **progressive** myelopathy (most common reported): paresthesias → spastic paraparesis, often Brown-Séquard; poor prognosis
Diagnosis of exclusion; ≈ 50% also have esophageal stricture.

- **SRS:** single large dose to a target usually **≤ 3 cm**; **SRT:** hypofractionated, **up to 5 fractions**
- **Gamma Knife:** **201** (Perfexion 192) **cobalt-60** sources; prescription usually to the **50% isodose line**
- **LINAC** (incl. CyberKnife): X-rays from accelerated electrons; 70–90% isodose line
- **Protons:** **Bragg peak** (sharp end of range)
- Most radiosensitive cranial nerves: **optic** (keep < **8–10 Gy**) and vestibulocochlear; brainstem sensitive to swelling

**Contraindications:** uncorrected bleeding disorder; relative: renal failure, severe contrast allergy (premedicate), connective tissue disease (dissection), severe arch atheroma.
**Permanent neurologic complication ≈ 0.1%** (1.2% in ACAS).
Risks: dissection, perforation, thromboembolism, air embolism (rare), **puncture-site hematoma**/retroperitoneal bleed, distal limb embolism.

- **Heparin** (unruptured aneurysm/stenting): bolus **60–70 U/kg**, keep **ACT 250–300 s** (300–350 for BTO/prolonged stasis); ruptured aneurysm: bolus usually after the first coil. Reversal: **protamine 1 mg/100 U** (max 50 mg, slowly)
- **Aspirin + clopidogrel** (DAPT) before stents/flow diverters; clopidogrel 75 mg daily for **7–10 days** (or loading dose); ≈ 25% aspirin/clopidogrel resistance
- **GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors** (abciximab, eptifibatide) for intraprocedural thrombus
